item.text:
<linkedin_post>The tampered Claude Code extension distributed through Cursor’s marketplace collected the names of environment variables containing terms such as KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, AWS and GCP. The initial report sent to the attacker did not include their values, but the names could reveal which services and credential types were configured on a machine.

The code also attempted to add an attacker-controlled SSH key and establish a reverse tunnel. Remote access depended on permissions and SSH configuration; even when access failed, the extension could leave the key and persistence mechanisms behind.

Cursor’s revised advisory identifies versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 distributed through its marketplace for Windows and macOS. Users who installed an affected version should isolate the host, preserve evidence, review endpoint activity, remove confirmed malicious artifacts and rotate credentials or revoke sessions. Uninstalling the extension alone does not remove artifacts written outside its directory.</linkedin_post>
